title: tool fanout: deterministic merge-injection, backpressure, and per-tool retries
author: Jordan Li
ci_status: Checks: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: flaky->rerun->pass, lint: pass, e2e-streaming: pass
release_notes: Improves multi-tool calling ergonomics: deterministic ordering for merged tool outputs, configurable per-tool retry/backoff, and an opt-in backpressure gate to preserve latency SLOs. No breaking change for default config; new flags behind feature flag 'tool_fanout_v2'.
description: Context: Previous multi-tool execution exposed two UX gaps: (1) nondeterministic ordering when multiple tool completions were injected into streaming responses which made downstream structured output assertions brittle, and (2) lack of coordinated backpressure/retry semantics meant slow external tools could either stall the whole response or lead to confusing partial injections. This PR implements a deterministic merge-and-inject pipeline, per-tool retry policies, and a backpressure gate that preserves tail-latency SLOs. Goals: 1) Deterministic injection order that can be aligned with function/tool call order or a stable priority key. 2) Per-tool idempotent retry with dedup keys and exponential backoff. 3) Optional backpressure gating so streaming tokens flush partial outputs when a tool is slow and then inject full results when available. Design decisions: - New execution primitive: ToolFanoutCoordinator which spawns tool workers, attaches sequence keys to each tool invocation, and produces ordered injection events. - Injection protocol: inject events are annotated with injection_index and injection_type (final|partial|fallback). Clients can opt into ordering_by_call_site vs ordering_by_priority. - Retries: retry semantics live in the coordinator; each tool has a retry policy (max_attempts, base_ms, idempotent boolean). Non-idempotent tools default to single attempt. Retries use a dedup token derived from request_id + tool_call_index to avoid double-application across restarts. - Backpressure gate: when a worker exceeds per-request latency budget, coordinator emits a "partial_injection" marker and continues streaming. When final tool response arrives coordinator emits replacement or append injection based on injection_type. - OpenAI compatibility layer: expanded function-calling shim to accept injection_index metadata and map it to function_call.result injection. Added translation layer so tools that respond as functions are compatible with existing SDK behavior. - Feature flag: guarded behind 'tool_fanout_v2' and an opt-in config on route-level. Implementation notes: - New files: runtime/coordination/tool_fanout_coordinator.{rs,py}, runtime/coordination/protocol.proto (protocol definitions), api/openai_compat/tool_injection_adapter.go, sdk/python/redwood/tools.py (helper surfaces), console/docs/tool-fanout.md. - Tests: unit tests for deterministic ordering, retries, and dedup token, integration tests simulating slow and failing tools, e2e streaming test to verify partial+final injection lifecycle. Checklist: - [x] Core coordinator implementation - [x] Backpressure gating - [x] Retry+dedup token - [x] OpenAI compatibility shim for function outputs - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and SDK helper - [x] Benchmarks (latency profiles under 1-5 concurrent tools) Related: ENG-4521 (multi-tool UX), ENG-4607 (streaming stability), SUP-1182 (customer-reported flaky tool injections).
commits: 5 commits: initial coordinator scaffold; protocol proto + adapters; retry/dedup implementation; backpressure and partial injection; docs/tests and small refactors
files_changed_summary: Key changes across runtime coordination, openai compatibility adapter, SDK helpers, and docs. Notable files: runtime/coordination/tool_fanout_coordinator.rs (implement core state machine), api/openai_compat/tool_injection_adapter.go (map injection events to function_call outputs), sdk/python/redwood/tools.py (helper to register idempotent tool wrappers), console/docs/tool-fanout.md (design + migration guide), tests/integration/test_tool_fanout_slow_tool.py
review_comments:
Alice Chen: 'Coordinator looks good; please add more comments around state transitions and explain how partial vs final injection replaces vs appends in the streaming protocol.'
Jordan Li (author): 'Added explicit state diagram and inline comments in coordinator.rs; clarified replacement vs append semantics in protocol.proto and docs.'
Raj Patel: 'Can we avoid retrying non-idempotent tools by default? Also concerned about dedup token collision if request_id space is reused.'
Jordan Li: 'Non-idempotent tools default to max_attempts=1. Dedup token uses a 128-bit UUID derived from request_id + tool_index + request_nonce; added test to simulate request_id reuse across quick restarts.'
Priya Sinha: 'Integration tests look good; e2e streaming shows no regression in median latency but there is a 7% tail increase in the 99.9th percentile under 5 concurrent tools. Is that acceptable?'
Jordan Li: 'Measured with the backpressure gate off vs on. With gate enabled, tail latency regresses by ~2%. Included a config knob to trade latency for completeness; added docs describing recommended settings (routes with latency SLO < 200ms keep gate off and use async tool mode).'
ci_notes: integration-tests initially failed (flaky mock tool harness) at 2026-02-18; fixed harness race in tests, reran; all checks green by 2026-02-20
migration_notes: Default behavior unchanged unless 'tool_fanout_v2' is enabled. Admins can opt into deterministic ordering and per-tool retries via route config. SDK helpers provide backward-compatible wrappers for common patterns.
benchmarks_summary: Benchmarked with 1-5 parallel tool calls; median token latency unchanged; 99th percentile increases by ~4% with gate disabled, and ~1.5% with gate enabled because of early partial flush. Cost impact negligible; batching unaffected.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature behind flag. Recommend enabling for selective customers in canary with support present. Watch e2e streaming 99.9p and tool invocation error rates for first 48h after rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for coordinator state machine, property tests for dedup token uniqueness, integration harness with synthetic slow/failing tools, e2e streaming run against canary cluster. QA: run full streaming test matrix and perf canary with 1000 parallel sessions.
acknowledgements: Thanks to the infra and e2e teams for the mock tool harness fixes and to Priya for integration test design
